answer: Time-locked skill harbor. Each identity must complete a distinct, verifiable apprenticeship task chain—months of logged work with a real mentor who co-signs outputs. Registration opens only after peer review of that portfolio by three unrelated reviewers, creating a slow pearl of accumulated track record. Attackers cannot mass-produce months of reviewed, cosigned work; each fake identity costs real mentor hours and sequential calendar time, and reviewer scrutiny exposes any hollow portfolio quickly, capping sybil creation at human mentoring bandwidth.
